_comment: The software-first CV. Every work highlight is copied verbatim from resume.cv.json and every project names a corpus entry, so lib/matt-site.nix fails the build on anything this file cannot find. The bio states only what the repository proves: the CI cache path, the pinned LTS kernel on legacy NVIDIA hosts, the mail archive and media relay.
title: Systems and software engineer
bio: I run a single-operator twenty-five-host NixOS fleet from one flake: an SSH certificate authority, per-host SOPS secrets, and the same checks in CI and before a deploy. CI builds only the affected hosts and pushes cache substitutes, and legacy NVIDIA hosts pin the 6.12 LTS kernel. The fleet self-hosts a PostgreSQL mail archive with full-text search, SQL endpoints and a web reader, and a media relay. Before software, four years of solar asset management.

work.name: Bountystash
highlights: Built and runs a twenty-five-host NixOS fleet as one flake: a feature list per host, a module per service, secrets encrypted with SOPS behind the fleet's own SSH certificate authority
Gated infrastructure changes with inventory-driven CI and a per-host module check, so a broken host definition fails before a deploy
Wrote a sentinel that logs job status, generation age, disk and PSI pressure every 15 minutes and pages when a service fails

Built a Go service, still in development; no external users yet: Postgres work_versions, exact hashes over canonical JSON, a quotient hash over the fields a reviewer sees, append-only events, and Go tests (github.com/shaoyanji/bountystash)

work.name: O3 Energy
highlights: Reconciled three feeds (meters, inverters, weather) for a USD 100M+ solar portfolio, turning missing readings into an explicit error budget, and built field capture so an inspection produced the same structured record as a meter reading

work.name: Fraunhofer ISE
highlights: Wrote C++ software for a heliostat interferometer that captured and processed optical measurement data
Implemented the analysis from a published paraboloid paper in Python, including 3D geometry tooling
